submitter: bugfix_357_component_identity lane — RFC_046 PHASE 0, ROUND 1 (a NEW round on a NEW finding, not a resubmission of the approved phase 1). Phase 1's stamp writer was APPROVED by this gate on 2026-08-22 18:02Z and rolled at 15:10Z. Measured today against the live database: it writes nothing. 820 page_components rows born since that roll, 0 stamped; 0 component_versions rows with change_source='render_stamp'; 0 'component version:' log lines in 24h, which is consistent with the resolver's SILENT early return. This round repairs the carriage that severed it, as a class fix rather than a key fix, and closes a second defect that un-severing would otherwise have ARMED.
rationale:
WHAT IS BROKEN. extractSectionFromMap (v3_site_actions.go:2835) rebuilds every section's metadata into a fresh map from a hand-written allow-list of six keys. rendered_template_sha — emitted by RenderComponentAction at :2559 and read by extractSectionsFromMetadata at :1391 — is not on that list, so it is dropped in silence at the hop between them. The save then reads an empty digest, resolveComponentVersionID takes its silent arm (src.renderedSHA == ""), and the INSERT writes NULL. The stamp was built, tested, council-approved, rolled, and inert.

THE EVIDENCE IS DISCONFIRMABLE, not an argument. Across live runs since the roll that carry the key somewhere in collected_data: 546 sections_metadata elements — 0 carry rendered_template_sha, 546 carry component_id, 546 carry content_data. The copy demonstrably runs; the key is demonstrably dropped. (An independent re-measure over a wider window the same day: 2,973 elements, same 0 / all.) Control on the other side: the pre-roll cohort is 0 of 1,146 stamped, as designed — nothing backfills.

WHY NOT JUST ADD THE KEY. Because that remedy has already been applied to this exact function and already failed. bugs_open/189 lost stored_slot_name at this same hop; it was fixed by adding that one key and pinning it with TestExtractSectionFromMap_ForwardsStoredSlotName — a good test, with a documented mutation, that asserts ITS OWN KEY is forwarded and therefore could not see the next one. No test file in this repo mentions rendered_template_sha at all. Three keys are in fact dropped today (rendered_template_sha, stripped_markdown_fields, copy_gate_findings) and nobody knew. So the fix is the CONTRACT: one declared carry list, one declared deny list with a stated reason per key, and a parity test that fails when a producer key is in neither or a save-read key is not carried.

AND ADDING THE KEY ALONE WOULD HAVE BEEN A REGRESSION, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. Layer 2's splice (:532) replaces a section's HTML with stored interactive bytes but left the rest of the section alone — including the RenderedTemplateSHA of the fresh render it just discarded. That is harmless only while the digest never arrives. Deliver it, and resolveComponentVersionID matches that digest against the hero component and stamps the hero version onto a whole interactive tool: not a missing answer but a false one, on precisely the rows bugs_open/357 is about (12 of the 22 were born today, so this is a live daily rate, not history). This round clears the discarded digest and adopts the stored row's own stamp instead.

AND A SECOND SEVERED HOP, previously unrecorded: RerenderPageSectionsAction's FRESH-RENDER entry (:746) never emitted the digest either, though :662 calls RenderTemplate and has it in hand 85 lines earlier. Phase 1 wired only that file's CARRY path. The rerender is the fleet's repair vehicle and the path that re-mints this population, so a page mended through a rerender came out less well-provenanced than one left alone.

WHAT THIS ROUND IS NOT. It does not fix bugs_open/357 and the submission says so in those words, on the precedent this lane set in round 2 after being rightly gated for claiming otherwise. Identity is still inferred at birth; the mint continues. This round makes the FACT the fix is made of actually reach the database, and stops that fact being false where it would have been. Nothing here reads component_version_id, so it still cannot change what any page serves.

plan.summary: Un-sever the RFC_046 identity stamp as a CLASS fix. One declared key contract for section metadata (carry list + deny list with reasons) replacing a hand-written allow-list; the same list used by both the top-level and nested-substep passes; the rerender's fresh-render producer emits the digest it already holds; Layer 2's carry arms make provenance describe the bytes they hand over rather than the bytes they discard; and a parity test that fails on an undeclared producer key or an uncarried save-read key. No migration, no livespec change, no new config key, no new reader of component_version_id.

edits.rationale: ONE definition of what travels with a section's bytes. The carry list is the six keys the hop already forwarded plus the two provenance keys the save already reads. The deny map names the keys a producer sets that deliberately do NOT travel, each with its reason: copy_gate_findings (per-render annotation, no reader at the save, and carrying it would persist finding arrays into collected_data a second time) and stripped_markdown_fields (whole-run diagnostic, not a per-section fact). The reason field is the point — a drop with a rationale is a decision; a drop with no entry anywhere is this bug. carrySectionMetaKey preserves today's per-key behaviour EXACTLY: component_id rendered with %v because producers supply both string and uuid.UUID; content_data taken whole when non-nil; every other key carried only when a non-empty string, so an absent fact stays absent — that distinction is load-bearing, since "" means unknown and unknown must reach the database as NULL rather than as a stamp nobody earned. It never overwrites, preserving the existing precedence of a top-level key over the same key recovered from a nested substep.
edits.sketch: var sectionMetadataCarryKeys = []string{...6 existing..., "rendered_template_sha", "component_version_id"}; var sectionMetadataDeniedKeys = map[string]string{"copy_gate_findings": "...reason...", "stripped_markdown_fields": "...reason..."}; func carrySectionMetaKey(dst, src map[string]interface{}, key string)

edits.rationale: Makes a section's provenance describe the bytes it has just been HANDED rather than the bytes it arrived with: clears the incoming digest, adopts the stored row's stamp. It is a function rather than two lines at the splice for a measured reason. The resolver swallows its own query errors and returns 'no stamp' on failure, so at the level of the whole action a section carrying a stale digest and a section carrying none write the SAME nil bind — the mutation that removes the clearing PASSED an action-level test on the first attempt. A guard in series stood in for the property under test. Extracting the decision makes it directly observable, and an AST test keeps the seam calling it.
edits.sketch: func adoptCarriedProvenance(s *SectionData, storedVersionID string) { s.RenderedTemplateSHA = ""; s.ComponentVersionID = storedVersionID }

edits.rationale: Replace the six hand-written key blocks — in BOTH the top-level pass and the nested-substep recovery loop, which was a second copy of the same list and would otherwise have had to be fixed twice — with loops over the declared carry list. Behaviour-identical for the six existing keys, which the pre-existing bugs_open/189 test still proves; the two provenance keys now survive. The 'is it complete yet' break condition becomes sectionMetaComplete over the same list, which is an optimisation only: a section with no content_data or no provenance is never complete and simply costs a scan of the remaining two substep shapes.
edits.sketch: for _, key := range sectionMetadataCarryKeys { carrySectionMetaKey(meta, m, key) }  // and the same over `nested`, guarded by if !sectionMetaComplete(meta)

edits.rationale: Emit rendered_template_sha from the RenderContext this loop already has: :662 calls RenderTemplate, which sets rc.RenderedTemplateSHA, and the entry is built from the same rc 85 lines later. This is the second severed hop and it is on the repair vehicle — carrying the stamp on the carry path while dropping it on the fresh-render path meant a page mended through a rerender came out less well-provenanced than one left alone. Empty stays ABSENT rather than becoming an empty string, so unknown still reaches the database as NULL.

The preload now selects component_version_id (COALESCE to '') and preservedSection carries it. The SPLICE arm calls adoptCarriedProvenance, so the discarded render's digest cannot reach the resolver and the stored row's own stamp travels with its bytes. The RE-APPEND arm sets ComponentVersionID from the stored row for the same reason; that arm cannot reach the database today because the INSERT resolves a version only when the section also has a component_id and a re-appended section has none — it is written so the two carry arms state the same thing, which is what stops the next edit reopening the gap on whichever one nobody is looking at. Existing mocks are unaffected: every current test returns an EMPTY preload row set, so the added column is never scanned by them.
edits.sketch: SELECT slot_name, rendered_html, content_data, COALESCE(component_version_id::text,'') ... ; case matchedIdx >= 0: ... adoptCarriedProvenance(&sections[matchedIdx], p.componentVersionID)

edits.rationale: The lockstep that closes the class. AST-based, not grep — reusing this package's own parsePackageFuncs, whose file states why: a text-matching rule makes COMMENTS load-bearing, and this test file's prose names every key in the contract. Producer half: every string key assigned into a declared producer's metadata variable must be carried or denied. Consumer half: every string key extractSectionsFromMetadata READS must be carried — that is the rule that would have caught this bug on the day the stamp was written. Both halves carry CONTROLS that fail loudly if the scan finds nothing (a renamed variable would otherwise make the test pass while checking nothing). Round-trip test drives a producer-shaped map through carrier and consumer in both the flat and nested shapes. MUTATIONS PROVEN TO KILL THEM: adding result["zz_undeclared_key"] to RenderComponentAction fails the producer half; deleting rendered_template_sha from the carry list fails the consumer half.

Layer 2's splice had NO test at all before this: every existing fixture returns an empty preload row set, which is why the false-stamp hazard was invisible. The direct pin asserts the decision (mutation: delete the clearing line — proven to fail it). The AST pin keeps the seam calling it (mutation: re-inline or remove the call — proven to fail it). The action-level pair pins the observable outcome AND its control: the spliced tool's stamp bind is nil, and the decoy version it declined is proven genuinely reachable in the same fixture by the paired test, because 'it did not take the decoy' means nothing if the decoy was never served. The stored stamp is empty in these fixtures deliberately — it is the live state of all 22 rows, and a carried stamp would short-circuit the resolver before it ever looked at the digest, hiding the field under test.
edits.sketch: expectSaveSlotReadsPreloading(mock, ..., layer2PreloadWith("hero", layer2ToolHTML, "")); mock.ExpectExec("INSERT INTO page_components").WithArgs(pageID, 1, AnyArg, "hero", AnyArg, AnyArg, AnyArg, nil)

edits.rationale: Parameterise the shared harness's Layer 2 preload so a test can stage a stored interactive row. The original signature is kept as a thin wrapper, so every existing caller is untouched, and the preload column set lives in one helper so a change to that query's SELECT list is not chased through two files. Mechanical; no existing expectation changes.

grounded_in: architecture_review/RFC_046 — RULED by the owner 2026-08-22, option 1: stamp identity at the point of production. This round is what makes that stamp actually reach the database.

LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-23: page_components created since the 2026-08-22 15:10:31Z roll = 820, of which stamped = 0. Control: pre-roll rows = 1,146, stamped = 0 (nothing backfills, as designed). component_versions with change_source='render_stamp' = 0.

LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-23, the disconfirming control: across runs since the roll carrying the key anywhere in collected_data, sections_metadata elements = 546, with rendered_template_sha = 0, with component_id = 546, with content_data = 546. The copy runs; the key is dropped.

LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-23: the bug file's own population query returns 22 rows, of which 12 were created 2026-08-23 — after the phase-1 roll. All position=1, slot_name='hero', component_version_id NULL. The population is self-renewing at roughly a dozen a day.

PRIOR ART, and the reason this is a contract fix: bugs_open/189 lost stored_slot_name at this same function, was fixed by adding one key, and pinned by TestExtractSectionFromMap_ForwardsStoredSlotName (v3_render_slot_name_test.go:158) which asserts only its own key. No test file in the repo mentions rendered_template_sha.

save_sections_component_version.go:92 — resolveComponentVersionID returns ("", false) with NO log line when src.renderedSHA == "", which is why 0 'component version:' lines in 24h of chassis logs is consistent with a severed carrier rather than with a resolver that is refusing.

LANDMINES.md — 'CORRECTING a page_components.slot_name makes the NEXT rebuild append the tool beside a freshly generated section'. Nothing in this round changes any slot_name, alters Layer 2's slot-name match, or touches pages.sections, so that landmine is not armed by it. The pin test asserts the rows written equals the incoming count.

BLAST RADIUS, measured rather than asserted: 7 live agent types consume sections_metadata (content-reviewer, page-build-handler, pageflow-builder, page-rebuild, page-rerender, site-work-orchestrator, tool-recreation-handler); collected_data averages 210KB per run and peaks at 2.6MB, which is why the fix declares keys rather than carrying everything by default.
plan.risks:
WHAT COULD GO WRONG, and what is already checked.

1. THE HOP NOW CARRIES TWO MORE KEYS INTO A PERSISTED ARTEFACT. sections_metadata is stored in orchestration_states.collected_data. The two added keys are a 64-char hex digest and a uuid, per section — negligible against a 210KB average payload that already contains every section's full rendered_html. Carry-everything was rejected precisely because it would not have this bound.

2. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE FOR THE SIX EXISTING KEYS. There should be none: carrySectionMetaKey reproduces each key's original condition exactly, including the %v rendering of component_id and the non-empty test on strings. The pre-existing bugs_open/189 test suite passes unchanged, and the round-trip test covers both the flat and nested shapes.

3. THE ADDED PRELOAD COLUMN COULD BREAK EXISTING MOCKS. Checked: the only fixture that feeds that query returns an EMPTY row set, so no scan runs; the sole AddRow on those column names is in a different package against a different query. The full actions suite passes at committed HEAD plus this change.

4. THE STAMP MIGHT STILL NOT FIRE AFTER THE ROLL. Possible — there may be a third producer nobody has found. The verification names its own disconfirming result: rows created after the next roll must carry a non-NULL component_version_id while the pre-roll cohort stays exactly 0. Still 0 means a producer is still severed, and the refusal branches will now log WHY, because they are finally reachable. A rising count on OLD rows would mean something is backfilling, which this design does not do.

5. A FALSE STAMP IS WORSE THAN NO STAMP, and this round is where that becomes possible. That is the F2 hazard above and the reason adoptCarriedProvenance exists. The residual risk is a carry path nobody has enumerated; the ones known are the compile hop, the rerender's two paths and Layer 2's two arms, all covered here. After the roll, the population's re-minted rows must still read component_version_id IS NULL — they are rewritten roughly daily, so that check answers within a day, and a population row appearing WITH a hero stamp is the signal to stop.

6. SCOPE. No opt-in field is added and no refusal is introduced, so the 2026-08-02 §2 remedy has nothing to attach to and RFC_022's trigger does not fire. No migration, no livespec object, no new config key: grep component_version_id in platform/livespec/livespec.go returns 0. The round-3 livespec objection therefore does not apply here either.
